name: Pyre-Hollow

civilization.name: The Ashwright Concord
civilization.notes: A vault-building culture that engineered cities into shielded caldera chambers; vanished when a global volcanic resurgence drowned their strongholds in ash and fire.

description: Pyre-Hollow turns slowly beneath a ceiling of storm, a great volcanic world wrapped in dense ochre clouds shot through with lightning. Below, continents of fused glass reflect the glow of supervolcano chains that erupt somewhere on the visible face at all times. The famous Hollow Plains stretch for thousands of kilometers, sand fused to mirror-smooth sheets by an ancient cataclysm, cracked now into vast tilting plates.

To stand on the glass is to feel the planet breathing. Thunder never stops; it rolls overhead in continuous volleys as storms feed on the heat rising from below. The air tastes of hot metal and ozone, and the horizon shimmers constantly, so that distant ruins seem to swim and reform like things seen through water.

The Ashwright Concord built their last cities inside cooled caldera chambers, sealing themselves against the worsening surface, and for a long time it worked. Then the mantle surged, chamber after chamber flooded with magma, and a spacefaring civilization ended not with an invasion but with geology. Their ruins still stand in the high calderas, and deep-scanner returns suggest something enormous, deliberate, and intact lies buried beneath the Hollow Plains themselves.

Dark crystal veins run through the Concord's ruins, and traces of exotic matter have been detected around the buried megastructure, enough to make corporations and governments alike sharpen their knives. The storms destroy most probes within days, and landers that survive the descent rarely survive the ascent. Whatever the Concord sealed under the glass, they spent their final generations making sure it stayed there.
